thread.title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Futures Point to Solidly Higher Start

title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Futures Point to Solidly Higher Start
text:
S&P 500 Futures Point to Solidly Higher Start 29-Oct-18 08:00 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +36.00. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +111.80.
U.S. futures are pointing to a solidly higher start, with the S&P 500 futures currently trading 36 points, or 1.4%, above fair value. The benchmark index enters today's session with a month-to-date loss of 8.8% after falling 1.7% on Friday.
Overseas, German Chancellor Angela Merkel will reportedly not run for reelection as CDU party chair, but will try to remain chancellor until the end of her term in 2021. The decision comes after the CDU and SPD lost a large number of votes in the state election in Hesse. Germany's DAX is currently up 1.9%, leading European markets higher.
In addition, reports indicate that China will lower its tax on auto purchases by 50.0%. Asian markets finished Monday mixed with China's Shanghai Composite (-2.2%) showing relative weakness.
Headlining earnings this week will be Facebook (FB) on Tuesday and Apple (AAPL) on Thursday. Other notable earnings reports include General Electric (GE), Pfizer (PFE), and Coca-Cola (KO) on Tuesday, General Motors (GM) on Wednesday, Starbucks (SBUX) on Thursday, and Alibaba (BABA) on Friday.
Investors will receive the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index (Briefing.com consensus +0.1%), at 8:30 AM ET. At the same time, the Personal Income (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) and Personal Spending (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) reports for September will be released.
In other markets, U.S. Treasury prices have decreased, pushing yields higher. The yields on the 2-yr and 10-yr Treasury notes are up two basis points each to 2.83% and 3.10%, respectively. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.1% to 96.48, and WTI crude is down 0.5% to $67.28/bbl.
In U.S. Corporate news: IBM (IBM 117.39, -7.40): -6.0% after agreeing to acquire open-source software company Red Hat (RHT 176.61, +59.93, +51.4%) for an all cash offer of $190 per share. Ford Motor (F 9.35, +0.37): +4.1% after China announced plans to lower its tax on auto purchases by 50.0%. General Motors (GM 34.02, +1.37) is also up, adding 4.2%.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region began the week on a mixed note. Japan's Nikkei -0.2%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng +0.4%, China's Shanghai Composite -2.2%, India's Sensex +2.2%. In economic data: Japan's September Retail Sales +2.1% year-over-year, as expected (last 2.7%) Australia's September HIA New Home Sales +1.1% month-over-month (last -2.9%) In news: China France's CAC +0.3%, UK's FTSE +1.7%, Germany's DAX +1.9%.
